newsitem.title: USA: GE reports record profits, revenues for quarter.
newsitem.headline: GE reports record profits, revenues for quarter.

text.p: General Electric Co. said Thursday that its third-quarter profits increased by 11 percent to a record $1.8 billion as nine of the company's 12 main businesses increased revenues.
The giant international conglomerate said its earnings for the three months ended Sept. 30 climbed to $1.788 billion, or $1.08 a share, from $1.610 billion, or 96 cents a share.
GE, based in Fairfield, Conn., said its revenues for the quarter grew by 16 percent to a record $20.0 billion from $17.3 billion

The company said the revenue increase resulted from income from the Summer Olympics televised by its NBC television network as well as from greater global activities and higher sales of spare parts and services.
The company said its GE Capital Services unit boosted its earnings 15 percent to $816 million, citing globalization and diversity of its 26 businesses.

Chairman John Welch said the company delivered another quarter of record results despite increasing global competition. "In addition, the businesses took significant steps to position the company for future growth," Welch added.
GE, which said NBC broadcast the Atlanta Olympics to a U.S. audience of 209 million, added that the network was expecting strong ratings for its new fall schedule.

GE also said that its Aircraft Engines division won more than 60 percent of orders for large commercial engines in 1996. The division also continued its growth by winning a 10-year servicing pact with USAir and acquiring controlling interest in CELMA, a Brazilian overhaul and maintenance firm.

Also during the quarter, GE Capital Services expanded its auto leasing operations by acquiring Japan's Marubeni Car Systems. Capital Services also expanded into the insurance and annuity products market by acquiring First Colony Corp.
For the first nine months of the year GE said its profits grew by 11 percent to $5.2 billion, or $3.15 a share, from $4.7 billion, or $2.79 a share.
Revenues for the year to date increased by 12 percent to $56.2 billion from $50.3 billion, the company said.
Cash generated from GE's operating activities through the first nine months was $5.4 billion, up from $2.4 billion, reflecting improvements in earnings and working capital.

GE said that as part of its $9 billion share repurchase plan, it bought back $674 million of its stock during the quarter to reach a total of 85 million shares, worth about $5.6 billion, purchased since December 1994.
GE's stock lost 62.5 cents to $92.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
